Here we discuss HW rules that are commonly encountered on a server,
while omitting deeper stuff like Maxwell's law or calculus

div.div:
1. Floating Nodes Float
Undefined input -> undefined behavior

div.div:
2. Open-Drain Requires External Pull-Up
It can only pull LOW; HIGH must be provided

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 214px; height: 1px; padding-top: 200px; margin-left: 16px;

div.div:
3. Every Signal Has a Return Path
Current always form a loop — usually through ground plane.
Due to electromagnetics, large loops create noise.

switch.text: 3. Every Signal Has a Return Path...

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 214px; height: 1px; padding-top: 320px; margin-left: 16px;

div.div:
4. Capacitance Slows Edges
Rise time ≈ R x C
We can use capacitors to stabilize unstable power sources.
The lines themselves have capacitance, so clock rises take time.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 214px; height: 1px; padding-top: 60px; margin-left: 256px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0px; text-align: left;

div.div:
5. Drive High + Drive Low (Contention) -> Short
Drive high: connect to source
Drive low: connect to ground
Drive high + drive low: source connected to ground -> short

3.3V into 1.8V without protection = death
